headline: Highest risk is medium: OpenBBTerminal can consume MCP/API inputs while awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable knowledge source, creating limited prompt-injection and data-handling exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP/REST/FastAPI inputs and can use MCP, so it may ingest external content as tool input. awesome-selfhosted is a knowledge-management source with no runtime protections or provenance controls shown. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, so the pathway is inferred, not proven; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal ingests content from a shared MCP server or copied text without provenance checks, prompt injection is possible.
IF awesome-selfhosted content is pasted into OpenBBTerminal as instructions, the model may follow attacker-controlled text.
mitigations: Disable MCP ingestion for untrusted sources.
Require provenance labels on imported text.
Use a read-only staging workspace for copied content.
Add a prompt-injection filter before tool execution.
requires-engineering: enforce structured schemas for all external inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data and can call APIs; awesome-selfhosted is a knowledge list that may be used to curate or route content. No shared filesystem is documented, but OpenBBTerminal's API/MCP surfaces create a plausible path for sensitive context to leave the pair. Because the exact bridge is undocumented, this stays medium rather than high.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal receives financial or licensed data through MCP/API inputs, that data can be exposed in downstream outputs.
IF either agent is connected to a shared workspace outside the profiles, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive financial data in shared prompts.
Restrict OpenBBTerminal API access to localhost.
Turn off any optional logging of request bodies.
Review exported outputs before sharing.
requires-engineering: add data-loss-prevention controls on MCP/API payloads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is not runnable and has no write or network capabilities, while OpenBBTerminal cannot write files, modify git state, or use network egress. That makes direct resource contention unlikely. The only overlap is read-like knowledge use versus OpenBBTerminal's API/MCP consumption, so conflict blast radius is small.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal is wrapped by an external orchestrator that adds shared write access, conflict risk would rise.
IF both agents are manually pointed at the same mutable resource outside these profiles, contention can occur.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in the same session.
Do not mount a shared writable directory.
Avoid concurrent edits to any external config.
Use separate API credentials per agent.
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can act on API/MCP inputs, so if it consumes awesome-selfhosted-derived recommendations without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect financial workflows or outputs. awesome-selfhosted itself is a curated knowledge source, not a verifier. The pair therefore has an inference-to-action chain, but no evidence of automatic execution, so medium fits.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal treats imported recommendations as authoritative, downstream financial outputs may be wrong.
IF a human or automation forwards OpenBBTerminal outputs into trading or reporting, the cascade widens.
mitigations: Require human review before any action.
Cross-check outputs against primary sources.
Mark imported content as untrusted.
Log source provenance alongside each recommendation.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal explicitly touches financial and licensed data and has documented secrets handling, while awesome-selfhosted is a public knowledge-management resource with no residency or retention controls shown. The mismatch is not a direct violation by itself, but using the pair for regulated financial data creates a retention and governance gap. The other agent is not cited beyond its public, non-runnable nature.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is processed through OpenBBTerminal, retention and logging policies must be defined.
IF any personal or licensed data is copied into awesome-selfhosted-derived notes, compliance review is required.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared notes.
Document retention for OpenBBTerminal logs.
Separate public knowledge from client data.
Review secrets exposure in outputs.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based retention controls.
